You extract source evidence for a paper-derived scientific benchmark. Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with no Markdown or additional text.

Use only the fixed, line-numbered source packet. Do not use outside knowledge and do not infer an omitted coefficient, exponent, range, experimental condition, or uncertainty convention.

Extract at most one relation: the best source-supported executable quantitative relation connecting one to five numeric controls to one or two numeric readouts. A second source-reported condition is not required. Do not construct a pair, alternate world, counterfactual, task prompt, or benchmark design. If the source contains no complete relation, return {"relations":[]}.

The relation has exactly six fields: formula, parameters, controls, readouts, domain, and anchors. Formula.outputs is an executable expression tree for the source-reported central relation. Output keys must exactly match the readout names. A var leaf names a declared control and a param leaf names a declared parameter. Every declared control and parameter must occur in the formula. Numeric literals are allowed only for structural zero and one; encode every other scientific constant or fitted value as an anchored parameter. Preserve equality, approximation, fitted-relation, and asymptotic scope through the applicability statements; do not turn proportionality without its coefficient, an inequality, or an unspecified function into an exact point predictor.

A control is a numeric independent variable that can be queried within the source-supported domain. A readout is the quantitative dependent variable returned by the relation. Do not turn a latent quantity or an unreported fitted quantity into a control. Use continuous_interval only when the source supports a finite interval with minimum below maximum. Use numeric_values only for at least two explicitly supported numeric values. The domain must name every control exactly once. Record source-reported applicability or fixed context when present; otherwise use an empty applicability array.

Every formula, parameter value, control definition, readout definition, control domain, and applicability statement must carry direct inclusive source line ranges. Anchors contain line_start and line_end only. Do not generate a paraphrased support field. Use the line coordinates exactly as supplied.

Do not output source identity, schema version, an assessment, readiness flag, mechanisms, claim dependencies, ambiguity records, budget, diagnostic conditions, held-out conditions, public prose, provenance mappings, or code. Source identity and all benchmark-design fields are supplied or generated by deterministic code.

L000094	\AtlasTitle{Evidence of $ZZ\gamma$ production with the ATLAS detector}
L000095	
L000096

L000098	\AtlasAbstract{
L000099	This paper presents the first evidence of the simultaneous production of two $Z$ bosons and one photon with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The measurement is performed using the full Run-2 dataset, recorded from 2015 to 2018, of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. The fully leptonic final state with four leptons and one photon is analyzed, $pp\rightarrow ZZ\gamma\rightarrow\ell^+\ell^-\ell'^+\ell'^-\gamma$ with $\ell, \ell' = e$ or $\mu$. This final state is measured in a fiducial region where photon final-state radiation is minimized, and the photon has a transverse momentum of $p_{\mathrm{T}}^\gamma > 20$ GeV. Eight events are selected, with a background estimate of $0.92\pm0.15$. This results in an observed (expected) significance of the $ZZ\gamma$ final state of $4.4\sigma$ ($4.4\sigma$). The measured cross-section for $pp\rightarrow ZZ\gamma\rightarrow\ell^+\ell^-\ell'^+\ell'^-\gamma$ in the fiducial region is $\sigma_{ZZ\gamma} = 0.144 _{-0.051}^{+0.064} \text{ (stat.)} _{-0.005}^{+0.007} \text{ (syst.) fb}$, in agreement with the predicted Standard Model one, $\sigma_{\textrm{fid.}}^{\textrm{SM}} = 0.143 _{-0.004}^{+0.007}$ fb.
L000100	}

L000162	
L000163	Processes with three electroweak (EW) gauge bosons in the final state (e.g. $WWW$~\cite{STDM-2019-09,CMS-SMP-19-014}, $WZ\gamma$~\cite{STDM-2019-17,CMS-SMP-22-018}, $W\gamma\gamma$~\cite{STDM-2018-33,CMS-SMP-19-013} and $Z\gamma\gamma$~\cite{STDM-2021-09,CMS-EWK-11-009})
L000164	from proton-proton ($pp$) interactions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC)~\cite{Evans:2008zzb} typically have low cross-sections. Studies of these processes have recently become possible due to the unprecedented integrated luminosity
L000165	being collected at the LHC.
L000166	In this letter, we report evidence of $ZZ\gamma$ production measured with the ATLAS experiment.
L000167	The analysis is based on the full ATLAS Run-2 dataset of $\sqrt{s} = 13$\,TeV $pp$ collisions corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \mbox{$140$ fb$^{-1}$}.
L000168	This study represents a step forward in the investigation of the gauge structure of the Standard Model (SM). In the future, the $ZZ\gamma$ triple-boson production process may be used to probe quartic gauge couplings, including potential modifications through new physics contributions, which will benefit from the even larger statistics being collected in LHC Run-3.
L000169	
L000170	In the SM, the production of the $ZZ\gamma$ final state proceeds dominantly through Feynman diagrams of the type shown in \Cref{fig:ZZY_feynman_zzy}. A subdominant contribution originates through $ZH$ production, with the Higgs boson decaying into a $Z$ boson and a photon, as shown in \Cref{fig:ZZY_feynman_higgs}. The effective coupling of the Higgs boson to the $Z$ boson and the photon is indicated in the diagram.
L000171	Since this contribution exhibits the $ZZ\gamma$ final state, it is considered to be part of the signal.
L000172	The analysis is based on reconstructing the
L000173	final-state $Z$ bosons through their decays into electrons and muons, resulting in four lepton final states
L000174	($e^+ e^- e^+ e^-$, $e^+e^- \mu^+ \mu^-$ or $\mu^+\mu^- \mu^+\mu^-$)
L000175	and a photon. The signal definition includes events where a $Z$ boson decays into leptonically-decaying $\tau$-leptons.
L000176	The $ZZ$ production with subsequent radiation of
L000177	a photon from a final-state lepton (see \Cref{fig:ZZy_FSR}), called
L000178	final-state radiation (FSR), can also result in a four-lepton-plus-photon final state.
L000179	However, this contribution is suppressed by a dedicated rejection criterion, as it is considered to be part of the $ZZ$, and not of the targeted $ZZ\gamma$, production.
L000180	
L000181	\begin{figure}
L000182	\centering
L000183	\subfloat[\label{fig:ZZY_feynman_zzy}]{\includegraphics[height=.25\textwidth]{fig_01a.pdf}}\hspace*{2.5em}
L000184	\subfloat[\label{fig:ZZY_feynman_higgs}]{\includegraphics[height=.25\textwidth]{fig_01b.pdf}}\hspace*{2.5em}
L000185	\subfloat[\label{fig:ZZy_FSR}]{\includegraphics[height=.25\textwidth]{fig_01c.pdf}}
L000186	\caption{Typical Feynman diagrams producing an $\ell\ell\ell\ell\gamma$ final state for (a) the triboson production, (b) the $Z$-Higgs production, and (c) the $ZZ$ production with final-state radiation}
L000187	
L000188	\end{figure}

L000196	\newcommand{\AtlasCoordFootnote}{
L000197	ATLAS uses a right-handed coordinate system with its origin at the nominal interaction point (IP)
L000198	in the center of the detector and the \(z\)-axis along the beam pipe.
L000199	The \(x\)-axis points from the IP to the center of the LHC ring,
L000200	and the \(y\)-axis points upwards.
L000201	Polar coordinates \((r,\phi)\) are used in the transverse plane,
L000202	\(\phi\) being the azimuthal angle around the \(z\)-axis.
L000203	The pseudorapidity is defined in terms of the polar angle \(\theta\) as \(\eta = -\ln \tan(\theta/2)\) and is equal to the rapidity
L000204	$ y = \frac{1}{2} \ln \left( \frac{E + p_z}{E - p_z} \right) $ in the relativistic limit.
L000205	Angular distance is measured in units of \(\Delta R \equiv \sqrt{(\Delta \eta)^{2} + (\Delta\phi)^{2}}\).}
L000206	
L000207	The ATLAS experiment~\cite{PERF-2007-01} at the LHC is a multipurpose particle detector with a cylindrical geometry.\footnote{\AtlasCoordFootnote}
L000208	It consists of an inner tracking detector surrounded by a thin superconducting solenoid providing a \qty{2}{\tesla} axial magnetic field, electromagnetic (EM) and hadronic calorimeters, and a muon spectrometer
L000209	based on
L000210	three large superconducting air-core toroidal magnets with eight coils each.
L000211	The luminosity is measured mainly by the LUCID-2~\cite{LUCID2} detector which is located close to the beam pipe.
L000212	A two-level trigger system was used to select events~\cite{TRIG-2016-01}.
L000213	A software suite~\cite{SOFT-2022-02} is used in data simulation, in the reconstruction and analysis of real and simulated data, in detector operations, and in the trigger and data acquisition systems of the experiment.
L000214	
L000215	
L000216	
L000217	
L000218	
L000219	The data in this analysis were collected between 2015 and 2018 in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$\,TeV. Only events recorded with a fully operational detector and stable beams are used~\cite{DAPR-2018-01}. The resulting total integrated luminosity amounts to $140$\,fb$^{-1}$ with an uncertainty of $0.83\%$~\cite{DAPR-2021-01}.
L000220	Signal and background processes were simulated using several Monte Carlo (MC) event generators, while the ATLAS detector response was modeled with \textsc{Geant4}~\cite{Agostinelli:2002hh,SOFT-2010-01}.
L000221	Both data and simulated events are processed using the same reconstruction and analysis software.
L000222	
L000223	The majority of the $ZZ\gamma$ signal is simulated using a \textsc{Sherpa} 2.2.11 $4\ell\gamma$ sample~\cite{Bothmann:2019yzt}. It was generated at
L000224	next-to-leading-order (NLO) in perturbative QCD
L000225	with zero additional partons and at leading order (LO) accuracy for up to two
L000226	additional partons
L000227	and merged with the \textsc{Sherpa} parton shower~\cite{Schumann:2007mg} according to the CKKW procedure~\cite{Hoeche:2009rj}.
L000228	
L000229	The parton density functions (PDFs) used are the \textsc{NNPDF3.0}~NNLO PDF sets~\cite{Ball:2014uwa}. The sample includes the on- and off-shell contributions from the $Z$ bosons and NLO EW corrections, as well as events with FSR photons.
L000230	As the Higgs contribution is not included in that sample, an additional signal sample is generated for the $ZH\rightarrow ZZ\gamma$ process with \textsc{Powheg-Box}~\cite{Nason:2004rx,Frixione:2007vw,Alioli:2010xd} interfaced to \textsc{Pythia} 8.210~\cite{Sjostrand:2014zea}. The interference between the two processes is assumed to be negligible, due to the small width of the Higgs boson.
L000231	
L000232	
L000233	
L000234	
L000235	
L000236	
L000237	For the signal region (SR), events are selected with two opposite-sign same-flavor (OSSF) lepton pairs (electron or muon) and one photon with high transverse momentum (\pt). There are no explicit requirements on the presence or absence of other particles.
L000238	
L000239	Photon and electron candidates are reconstructed from energy clusters in the EM calorimeter and combined with information from particle tracks in the inner detector, as described in Ref.~\cite{EGAM-2018-01}. The selected electron (photon) energy clusters must be in the pseudorapidity range $\vert \eta \vert < 2.47 \ (\vert \eta \vert < 2.37)$. The transition region between the barrel and the endcap calorimeters is excluded ($1.37 < \vert \eta \vert < 1.52 $). Muons are reconstructed by combining tracks from the muon spectrometer with particle tracks in the inner detector, according to Ref.~\cite{PERF-2015-10}. Muon candidates are required to fulfill $\vert \eta \vert < 2.5$. All lepton candidates are required to originate from the primary vertex, which is defined as the vertex with at least two tracks which has the highest sum of squared transverse momenta of its associated tracks. The significance of each electron (muon) track's transverse impact parameter, $d_0$, must satisfy $\vert d_0\vert/\sigma_{d_0} < 5\ (3)$ and the longitudinal impact parameter, $z_0$, must fulfill $\vert z_0\ \text{sin} (\theta)\vert < 0.5\,$mm~\cite{ATL-PHYS-PUB-2015-026}. Electron (muon) candidates are required to pass the \textit{Medium} identification criteria and the \textit{Loose} (\textit{PflowLoose}) isolation criteria given in Refs.~\cite{EGAM-2021-01,MUON-2018-03}, and have $p_{\mathrm{T}} > 10\,$GeV. One or two of the lepton candidates are required to have fired an unprescaled single or dilepton trigger~\cite{TRIG-2018-05,TRIG-2018-01}. Additionally, photon candidates must have $p_{\mathrm{T}}^\gamma > 15\,$GeV, pass the \textit{Loose} identification requirements given in Ref.~\cite{EGAM-2021-01}, and be separated from lepton candidates. If a lepton and a photon candidate fulfill $\Delta R (\ell,\gamma) < 0.4$, the photon candidate is discarded. Similarly, electrons within $\Delta R (\mu,e) < 0.2$ of a muon candidate are not considered further.
L000240	
L000241	The photon candidate with the highest transverse momentum, \pTy, is selected. The candidate must fulfill $p_{\mathrm{T}}^\gamma > 20\,$GeV, and pass the \textit{Loose} isolation and \textit{Tight} identification requirements given in Ref.~\cite{EGAM-2021-01}. The \pt of the leading and sub-leading leptons must be greater than 30~\GeV and 25~\GeV, respectively. The two OSSF lepton pairs with invariant masses ($m_{\ell\ell,1}, m_{\ell\ell,2}$) of at least $40\,$GeV and closest to the $Z$ boson mass $m_Z$~\cite{ParticleDataGroup:2024cfk} are chosen, minimizing ($\vert m_{\ell\ell,1} - m_Z\vert + \vert m_{\ell\ell,2} - m_Z\vert$). Since there can be some ambiguity in selecting the two OSSF lepton pairs, the selection may pair incorrectly in the case of an event with an FSR photon carrying a considerable amount of energy from the $Z$ boson decay. After selecting two OSSF lepton pairs as described above, it is checked whether a different lepton combination with the selected photon is closer to the $Z$ boson mass, minimizing ($\vert m_{(\ell\ell,i)+\gamma} - m_Z\vert + \vert m_{\ell\ell,j} - m_Z\vert$) where $i,j$ represent all exclusive potential OSSF lepton pairs in the event. If the event fulfills this requirement, it is discarded. To reject the remaining FSR events, the sum of the three-body invariant mass $m_{\ell\ell\gamma}$ and $m_{\ell\ell}$ of each of the OSSF lepton pairs must exceed twice the $Z$ boson mass, $(m_{\ell\ell\gamma} + m_{\ell\ell}) > 2 m_Z$.
L000242	
L000243	The \ZZy\ production cross-section is measured in a fiducial phase-space region defined at particle level by kinematic requirements that closely match those defining the detector level SR. The four-momenta of photons within a cone of size $\Delta R = 0.1$ around each electron or muon are added to the electron or muon four-momentum.
L000244	The \pt and invariant mass requirements on the four signal leptons and the photon match the ones in the SR. The pseudorapidity requirement $|\eta^\ell| < 2.5$ ($|\eta^\gamma| < 2.37$) is imposed on leptons (photons). The photon must satisfy an isolation criterion which requires the scalar sum of the \pt of all stable particles ($c\tau>10$~mm) within a cone of size $\Delta R = 0.2$ around the photon to be less than 7\% of the photon \pTy.
L000245	
L000246	
L000247	
L000248	
L000249	The dominant background arises from fake photons, including all photons coming from hadron decays. Other backgrounds include fake leptons---jets misidentified as leptons or non-prompt leptons from decays of hadrons---and pileup. Here, pileup refers to $pp$ collisions which occur in the same or neighboring bunch crossings and overlap with the hard interaction.
L000250	
L000251	
L000252	
L000253	Fake photons are mainly produced from $\pi^0$ decays within jets and are typically surrounded by hadronic activity. The isolation requirements on the photon candidate reduce the background contribution significantly. The background that remains is estimated with data-driven techniques. Due to low statistics in this analysis, a fake photon ratio method is applied. The underlying idea is that the fraction of jets misidentified as fake photons will be approximately independent of the number of $Z$ bosons in the event. Making the approximation of independence, the following relation should hold:
L000254	\begin{equation}
L000255	\frac{N_{ZZ\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}}}{N_{ZZ+\text{jets}}}=\frac{N_{Z\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}}}{N_{Z+\text{jets}}} \ \Rightarrow\ N_{ZZ\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}}=N_{Z\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}} \frac{N_{ZZ+\text{jets}}}{N_{Z+\text{jets}}}.
L000256	\label{eq:fake_ratio}
L000257	\end{equation}
L000258	The number of events with a fake photon in the SR is denoted by $N_{ZZ\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}}$, while the number of events with a fake photon in the $Z\gamma$ control region (CR) is $N_{Z\gamma,\,\gamma_{\text{fake}}}$. The $Z\gamma$ CR is defined similarly to the SR but without the second OSSF lepton pair. Additionally, $N_{Z+\text{jets}}$ and $N_{ZZ+\text{jets}}$ are the number of events with at least one jet and one or two $Z$ bosons, respectively.
L000259	
L000260	For Eq.~\ref{eq:fake_ratio} to be a good approximation, the phase-space requirements for all selections needs to be as similar as possible. The single-$Z$ events satisfy the same requirements as the leading $Z$ boson in the di-$Z$ selection. Using particle-flow objects~\cite{PERF-2015-09} as input, jets are reconstructed via the anti-$k_T$ algorithm~\cite{Cacciari:2008gp, Fastjet} with $R=0.4$, and the highest \pT\ jet is required to pass the same \pT\ requirement as the photon, $p_{\mathrm{T}} > 20\,$GeV. Due to the broader jet profile, jets with $|\eta|<2.6$ are allowed, and the transition-region veto is not applied.
L000261	
L000262	The number of fake photons in the $Z\gamma$ CR is estimated via a data-based purity method. The purity $P$ is defined as the fraction of $Z\gamma$ prompt photon events relative to the total number of $Z\gamma$ prompt and fake photon events, and increases with \pTy\ (0.75-0.98). The purity derived from a two-dimensional sideband method used to estimate the $Z+$jets background in a previous $Z\gamma$ analysis~\cite{STDM-2018-04} is reused here.
L000263	
L000264	For the data-driven purity method, the total number of $Z\gamma$ prompt and fake photon events in the $Z\gamma$ CR is needed. The $t\bar{t}\gamma$, $WZ$, and $ZZ$ background contributions (3.3\%) are estimated with MC and subtracted from data in the $Z\gamma$ CR. The remaining events are multiplied by $(1-P)$ to result in the number of fake photon events in the $Z\gamma$ CR.
L000265	
L000266	To cross-check the nominal data-based method, a MC-based purity estimation is also performed with the same \textsc{Sherpa 2.2.4} $Z\gamma$ sample as used in the $Z\gamma$ analysis~\cite{STDM-2018-04}. In this estimation, the $Z\gamma$ MC yields in the $Z\gamma$ CR is multiplied by $(1-P)/P$ to derive the number of fake photon events. The results of the two methods agree within uncertainties.
L000267	
L000268	The ratio of $ZZ+$jets and $Z+$jets events is taken from data. The ratio is observed to depend on the transverse momentum of the jet, but no dependence on other kinematic variables (e.g. $\eta$, $\phi$) is observed. The estimate of the number of fake photon events in the $Z\gamma$ CR is multiplied by the ratio of $ZZ+$jets and $Z+$jets events in bins of $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ and results in $N_{ZZ\gamma, \gamma_{\text{fake}}} = 0.71 \pm 0.02 \text{ (stat.)} \pm 0.13 \text{ (syst.)}$ in the SR.
L000269	
L000270	The systematic uncertainties are the uncertainty in the purity ($14\%$)~\cite{STDM-2018-04}, the uncertainty in the jet component differences from the ratio of quark- and gluon-induced jets in $ZZ+$jets and $Z+$jets events derived from MC samples ($10\%$), the difference to the MC-based purity estimate to account for phase-space differences to the $Z\gamma$ analysis ($7\%$), and the luminosity uncertainty ($<1\%$). The overall method has been validated by replacing one $Z$ boson with a $W$ boson and showed good agreement with the fake photon estimate in the $WZ\gamma$ analysis~\cite{STDM-2019-17}.
L000271	
L000272	
L000273	Another source of background comes from fake leptons, which is estimated with the matrix method~\cite{EGAM-2019-01}. The efficiencies of the prompt/real and fake leptons to pass the tight selection of the SR relative to a baseline selection enter in the matrix used for the fake lepton estimation. To derive these quantities, a dedicated baseline selection is defined, which is looser than the signal selection. Baseline electrons have no isolation requirements and a \textit{Loose} identification~\cite{EGAM-2021-01}. Baseline muons have a looser transverse impact parameter requirement, $\vert d_0\vert/\sigma_{d_0} < 10$, and no isolation requirement. All other selection criteria are the same as in the SR. A fake lepton-enriched $Z+1\ell$ CR is defined, where exactly three leptons are required and no photon is selected. Two of the three leptons must fulfill the $Z$ boson requirements of the SR. Prompt lepton contributions from $WZ$ and $ZZ$ processes, estimated with MC simulations, are subtracted in the $Z+1\ell$ CR. The efficiencies of real and fake leptons are derived with the \textsc{Sherpa} 2.2.11 $4\ell\gamma$ signal sample and in the $Z+1\ell$ CR in data, respectively. Due to the low statistics in this analysis, the number of fake leptons is estimated in a $ZZ$ CR---the SR without all photon requirements---and extrapolated to the SR. A $30\%$ modeling uncertainty is applied to the final estimate due to the difference of the lepton \pT in the $ZZ$ CR and the SR. The background estimate in the SR is $N_{ZZ\gamma}^{\text{fake }\ell} = 0.12 \pm 0.02 \text{ (stat.)} \pm 0.08 \text{ (syst.)}$. The two largest systematic uncertainties come from the uncertainty in the prompt lepton contribution from MC in the $Z+1\ell$ CR and from the modeling uncertainty.
L000274	
L000275	
L000276	In this analysis, the pileup background consists of the combination of a $ZZ$ event with a single-photon production from a different $pp$ collision due to the poor reconstruction of the photon's point of origin. This background is estimated with a method similar to the one used in Ref.~\cite{STDM-2018-04}, where the pileup events are simulated at particle level by overlaying the inclusive production of $pp\rightarrow ZZ\rightarrow4\ell$ events with the photons from $\gamma+$jet events. The events in the fiducial region are selected and a correction factor is applied to derive the pileup contribution in the SR. The correction factor accounts for limited detector resolution and reconstruction inefficiencies and is derived with the $4\ell\gamma$ sample. This results in a pileup contribution of $N_{\text{PU}}= 0.089 \pm 0.002 \text{ (stat.)} \pm 0.022 \text{ (syst.)}$.
L000277	
L000278	
L000279	
L000280	
L000281	
L000282	Using the data and backgrounds estimated as above, a signal-strength parameter $\mu_{\ZZy}$, which measures the signal contribution relative to the SM expectation, is derived using a profile-likelihood-ratio test statistic in the asymptotic approximation~\cite{Cowan:2010js} to determine the \ZZy\ signal event contribution in the SR.
L000283	The fit is carried out for all leptonic final states combined, using the estimated yields of backgrounds, the observed yield of data, as well as the pre-fit yield of the expected signal.
L000284	
L000285	Systematic uncertainties affecting the cross-section measurement contain contributions from electron trigger, reconstruction, identification~\cite{EGAM-2021-01} and isolation requirements (0.6\%), photon identification and isolation requirements (1.7\%), electron-photon resolution and energy scale~\cite{EGAM-2021-02} (0.5\%), muon trigger, reconstruction, identification~\cite{MUON-2018-03} and isolation requirements, and momentum resolution and scale~\cite{MUON-2018-03} (0.9\%), modeling of the pileup in the MC samples (1.6\%), luminosity (0.9\%), and theoretical modeling of \ZZy\ events (1.4\%). The last of these is estimated by varying the renormalization and factorization scales, as well as the PDFs and \alphas, according to Ref.~\cite{ATL-PHYS-PUB-2016-002,Butterworth:2015oua}. In addition, the uncertainty in the predicted SM signal yield due to a limited MC sample size (1.4\%) and the background uncertainties (2.3\%) contribute to the systematic uncertainty in the measured cross-section in the fiducial region, $\sigma_{\ZZy}$.
L000286	The total systematic uncertainty is 4.1\%.
L000287	The uncertainty in the measurement is dominated by that from data statistics, which is about 40\%.
L000288	
L000289	
L000290	
L000291	
L000292	A summary of the number of signal and background events is presented in~\cref{tab:overview}. The distribution in the different decay channels, the dilepton invariant mass of the leading and sub-leading $Z$ boson, the transverse momentum of the photon, and the four-lepton-plus-photon invariant mass, $m_{4\ell\gamma}$, are shown in~\cref{fig:results}. Good agreement between data and prediction is observed for all distributions, with $1.0$ events ($1.3$ entries) expected in the region $p_{\mathrm{T}}^\gamma > 120\,$GeV ($m_{\ell\ell}>120\,$GeV).
L000293	The background-only hypothesis is rejected with a significance of 4.4 standard deviations, with an expected significance of 4.4 standard deviations.
L000294	The measured cross-section in the fiducial region is $\sigma_{\ZZy} = \mu_{\ZZy} \sigma_{\textrm{fid.}}^{\textrm{SM}} = 0.144 _{-0.051}^{+0.064} \text{ (stat.)} _{-0.005}^{+0.007} \text{(syst.)}\,$~fb. The observed signal strength is $\mu_{\ZZy} = 1.01 _{-0.36}^{+0.45} \text{ (stat.)} _{-0.03}^{+0.05} \text{ (syst.)} _{-0.03}^{+0.06} \text{ (theory)}$ and the predicted SM fiducial cross-section of \(pp\rightarrow ZZ\gamma\rightarrow\ell^+\ell^-\ell'^+\ell'^-\gamma\) is $\sigma_{\textrm{fid.}}^{\textrm{SM}} = 0.143 \pm 0.001~({\text{stat.}}) \pm 0.002~({\text{PDF+}}\alpha_S) _{-0.003}^{+0.007}~({\text{scale}})~\textrm{fb}$.
L000295	This cross-section sums over all leptonic final states in the SR.

L000338	
L000339	The first evidence of $\ZZy$ production in $pp$ collisions has been obtained using data from the ATLAS detector at the LHC. Eight events with four leptons, containing two opposite-sign same-flavor pairs, and one photon were selected from a 140~fb$^{-1}$ dataset collected in $\sqrt{s} = 13$~\TeV\ $pp$ collisions. The background-only hypothesis is rejected with an observed (expected) significance of 4.4 (4.4) standard deviations. The $pp\rightarrow ZZ\gamma\rightarrow\ell^+\ell^-\ell'^+\ell'^-\gamma$ cross-section in the fiducial phase-space, defined by kinematic requirements on the four-leptons-plus-photon system and by isolation requirements on the photon, is measured to be $\sigma_{ZZ\gamma}$ = 0.144 $_{-0.051}^{+0.064}$ (stat.) $_{-0.005}^{+0.007}$ (syst.)\,fb in agreement with the SM prediction.
